instructions: Put the glass noodles in a bowl and cover them with warm water. Put the shiitake in a second bowl and cover them with very hot water. Leave both for 10 minutes while you prep.
Slice the carrots into thin half-moons. Thinly slice the celery. Slice the cabbage into 1-inch strips. Cut the tofu into 1/2-inch cubes.
Finely chop the cilantro stems and the garlic. Crush the peppercorns with a mortar and pestle or the bottom of a pan, then mash everything together into a rough paste.
Drain the noodles and cut them a few times so they're shorter. Drain the shiitake, cut off the stems and slice the caps thinly.
Pour the broth into a large pot and add the paste and the tamari. Cover and bring it to a boil over medium-high heat.
Add the carrots, celery and shiitake and boil for 2 minutes.
Add the cabbage, tofu and noodles and cook for 1 minute, until the cabbage is just wilted.
Take the pot off the heat. Taste it, and add a splash more tamari if it's flat.
Serve right away in bowls. The noodles keep soaking up broth, so this soup is best eaten the day it's made.
method_notes: Hungry in Thailand's tom jued (unrated) is a fallback lead, and Cup of Yum's version (0 reviews) is the same recipe: a pounded garlic, cilantro root and peppercorn paste in a light broth with carrots, celery, shiitake, Chinese cabbage, egg tofu and glass noodles, all cooked about 3 minutes. Adapted for gluten-free: bouillon cubes become gluten-free vegetable broth, oyster sauce becomes gluten-free tamari, and egg tofu becomes soft tofu. Cilantro stems stand in for the hard-to-find roots. Check the glass noodle and broth labels for gluten.
